title: Service Pressure Lens: error taxonomy, deferred failures, and new dashboard mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We lack a consistent way to categorize and visualize inference failures that are driven by service pressure (queueing, GPU saturation, kernel timeouts) vs. model/runtime errors (decoding failures, OOM, invalid responses) vs. transport errors (HTTP/gRPC codes, client timeouts). Current dashboards conflate counts and hide important mitigation signals (retryable vs non-retryable, upstream vs model).

Goal: Deliver a failure taxonomy and a small set of dashboards that let oncall/engineers answer: (1) Is the observed error spike caused by overload or model regression? (2) Which model versions and routes are showing tail-latency correlated with a specific failure type? (3) Which failures are transient/retryable vs permanent?

Scope:
- Define a failure taxonomy for inference paths (timeouts, overload, model runtime errors, model output/decoding, transport 4xx/5xx, gRPC statuses).
- Instrument tracing hooks and span attributes to emit failure_reason, failure_stage, retryable, model_version, kernel_id, gpu_id, queue_ms.
- Add structured log fields for model_error_code, tokenization_error, kv_cache_miss.
- Emit new metrics: redwood.inference.errors_by_type, redwood.inference.queue_depth, redwood.inference.kernel_time_ms, redwood.inference.kv_cache_miss_ratio.
- Build dashboard panels: failure-type heatmap by route/model, p50/p95/p99 latency overlays with error-rate, per-model failure rate over time, root-cause trace waterfall for representative failures, and SLO burn-by-failure-type.

Non-goals: Automated remediation (will be follow-up), full enterprise incident playbook rewrite (partial updates only).

Detection signals (initial mapping):
- Client timeouts: high 499/HTTP client_aborts, span.duration close to client timeout with cancel flag, logs with "context canceled" or gRPC code 1 (CANCELLED).
- Backend/kernel timeouts: span with failure_reason=kernel_timeout, kernel_time_ms > configured kernel_timeout, GPU watchdog traces, retry attempts with same model kernel id.
- Overload (queueing): sustained queue_depth > 0, increasing enqueued_time metric, GPU_util > 85% with rising queue_depth, concurrent inflight requests metric.
- Model runtime errors: logs with model_error_code (e.g., OOM, NAN, decode_error), spans with error=true and model_version tag, tokenization_error counts.
- Model output errors: structured output schema validation failures, function-calling parse errors, low-likelihood scoring anomalies captured by quality monitors.
- Transport errors: HTTP 4xx/5xx mapping by route, gRPC status codes (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, UNAVAILABLE, INTERNAL).

Dashboard sketches (panels):
- Failure Heatmap: rows=route, cols=failure_reason, cell=color=rate change, tooltip=top contributing spans/trace links.
- Service Pressure Timeline: stacked metrics (queue_depth, gpu_util, kernel_time_ms) with overlaid p99 latency and error_rate.
- Model Version Slice: per-model failure rate timeseries, with shaded canary window and rollout markers.
- Trace Waterfall Example: curated sample traces for each failure_reason with span-level annotations (enqueued_ms, kernel_ms, retry_count).
- SLO Burn by Failure Type: rolling SLO burn and projected breach probability per failure_reason.

Acceptance Criteria:
1) Taxonomy doc reviewed and merged in Confluence with owner and examples for each bucket.
2) Instrumentation merged that attaches failure_reason and failure_stage to inference root spans and relevant child spans.
3) Logs pipeline writes model_error_code and tokenization_error as structured fields and they appear in the logs backend within 10 minutes of ingestion.
4) Metrics redwood.inference.errors_by_type and redwood.inference.queue_depth are emitting and visible in the metrics backend for at least two routes.
5) Dashboard deployed to the Console with the five panels above; each panel links to at least one representative trace or log query.
6) Runbook appendix (short) created describing investigator steps per taxonomy bucket.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (this ticket): finalize taxonomy, instrument span tags (root + kernel), add basic metrics, create dashboard skeleton, add sample traces.
- Phase 2 (follow-ups): tail-sampling adjustments, enrichment of logs in pipeline, alert tuning and playbook.

Rollout considerations and trade-offs:
- Tag cardinality: adding model_version and kernel_id increases cardinality. To limit costs we will only emit model_version on error spans and sample 1% of success spans with model_version.
- Sampling: tail-sampling to retain error traces with full span trees; use low-rate random sampling for successful requests to keep storage bounded.
- Metrics cardinality: errors_by_type will be aggregated by route/service/model_cohort (coarse) instead of exact model_version for traffic-level dashboards.
- Latency-effect on instrumentation: adding span tagging is low-cost but log enrichment requires careful batching to avoid added latency to the request path; use async log write patterns.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Failure+Taxonomy+Service+Pressure (draft)
- Draft dashboard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2124
- Tracing library changes (branch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/observability/failure-taxonomy
